fieldMarks: Short, stout body with a broad, disproportionately large head; 8-12 cm long.
Terrestrial adults are grey to black, sometimes with clusters of small bluish-white flecks on the back and tail and often a white edge along the top of the tail.
Paedomorphic (gilled, aquatic) adults keep larval form, with light and dark belly stripes and distinctive yellow ventral stripes that remain as remnants for a time after metamorphosis.
Facultatively paedomorphic: both terrestrial and aquatic adult forms occur.
behavior: Active at any hour but mostly at night; moves on moist, cool nights; relatively sedentary near its natal pond or the forest around it (adults average about 170 m to breeding ponds).
Breeds in winter in the south and fall in the north; adults leave breeding ponds by mid-May (March in South Carolina).
Adults eat earthworms, arthropods, aquatic insects and tadpoles; larvae eat zooplankton and sometimes other Ambystoma larvae.
habitat: Usually near breeding ponds in pine flatwoods, floodplains and bottomland hardwood forest; terrestrial adults live in burrows or under logs in damp places; breeds in shallow fishless ponds with abundant vegetation; paedomorphs occur in permanent ponds.
range: NatureServe lists it in the southeastern and south-central US (Virginia and the Carolinas to Florida, west to Texas and north to Illinois, Indiana, Missouri and Kentucky); not recorded for Canada.
